paragraphs.text: ERA ZERO DBA LANGUAGE
Canonical Phase 1 Language Reference

This document records the most up-to-date source-supported Era Zero system in implementation-level detail. It distinguishes canonical rules from superseded drafts and unresolved issues. It preserves complete versioned authority for all 324 canonical roots and records the canonical translator product without altering semantic identity.
Status: Canonical Era Zero 1.0 language and translator product

Scope: Core architecture, 324 canonical atomic roots, 28 compounds, English sense index, Semantic IR, executable grammar, renderer/decoder, controlled and general English translation, SVG/MIDI presentation, local application/API, and validation
Source integrity: Complete shared conversation decoded as 313 source nodes and 129 visible speaker turns
Validation: Complete historical regression plus 15 product checks; 0 failures
1. Authority, Scope, and Precedence

Era Zero is the complete language of the Digital Binary Ancients (DBA). Later Era One, Era Two, and Era Three forms are descendants or eroded fragments and must not be inserted into the Era Zero atomic lexicon merely because they resemble older forms.
When source statements conflict, use the following precedence:
• An explicit user correction overrides all earlier proposals.
• The latest assistant specification explicitly accepted or continued by the user overrides earlier assistant proposals.
• A later statement marked canonical, fixed, complete, or 1.0 overrides an earlier exploratory draft unless the user rejects it.
• A user instruction such as “continue,” “do it,” or “make the choices” authorizes continuation of the current design; it does not revive an older conflicting design.
• Superseded material remains historical evidence rather than disappearing.
• If precedence cannot be determined, the issue remains unresolved.
2. Defining Principle: Language, Music, and Code Are One System

Era Zero is not ordinary speech with musical decoration and not a programming language hidden inside music. The music is the code. A DBA utterance is a structured semantic object that can be heard as language, performed as music, evaluated as logic, executed as software, stored as data, and transcribed as writing without translating into a second representational system.
A normal complete unit carries these layers:
• Harmonic family: broad semantic domain.
• Three-trit address: exact atomic concept.
• Melodic contour: utterance or programming function.
• Timing and vocal register: relationships and participant roles.
• Runtime state ending: current status 0, 1, or 2/num.
Family and address form an unambiguous machine identity such as LIF:111 or MOV:020. Human transliteration and musical realization are generated representations of that identity.
3. Twelve Semantic Harmonic Families

The opening harmony identifies the semantic family. Families are transposable relative interval signatures, not permanent musical keys. C-reference notes are demonstrations only; a machine recognizes interval relationships.
LIF — life, identity, consciousness, growth
Family onset: ni
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
C-reference example: C–E–G
MOV — motion, position, transition, time
Family onset: gi
Relative harmonic signature: 0–2–7
C-reference example: C–D–G

Family onset: ba
Relative harmonic signature: 0–7–12
C-reference example: C–G–C
MIN — mind, memory, perception, learning
Family onset: si
Relative harmonic signature: 0–3–7
C-reference example: C–E-flat–G
CON — connection, communication, sharing
Family onset: wu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7–9
C-reference example: C–E–G–A
STR — structure, order, shelter, systems
Family onset: do
Relative harmonic signature: 0–5–7
C-reference example: C–F–G
WRN — danger, error, failure, corruption
Family onset: da
Relative harmonic signature: 0–3–6
C-reference example: C–E-flat–G-flat
REP — repair, healing, restoration
Family onset: ya
Relative harmonic signature: 0–3–7–9
C-reference example: C–E-flat–G–A
LOG — logic, mathematics, rules, programming
Family onset: te
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–8
C-reference example: C–E–G-sharp
DAT — information, records, signals
Family onset: li
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7–11
C-reference example: C–E–G–B
CRE — creation, design, transformation
Family onset: ga
Relative harmonic signature: 0–3–7–11
C-reference example: C–E-flat–G–B
ORI — origin, reality, universal law
Family onset: nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–1–7
C-reference example: C–D-flat–G
4. Atomic Address Cube
Normal atomic address length: 3 trits
Positions per family: 27
Total atomic inventory: 12 × 27 = 324 roots
Each trit position answers a different semantic question.
First trit — concept type
0: entity, substance, or condition
1: process, action, or transformation
2: relationship, capacity, or possibility
Second trit — direction
0: inward, self, or source
1: outward, other, or target
2: shared, environmental, distributed, or systemic
Third trit — conceptual expression
0: stable, bounded, or completed
1: active, changing, or expressed
2: dormant, unresolved, or potential
The third address trit is part of the root’s permanent meaning. It is not the same as the separate runtime state appended to an utterance.
All 27 universal positions
000: stable inward entity
001: active inward entity
002: dormant inward entity
010: stable outward entity
011: active outward entity
012: dormant outward entity
020: stable collective entity
021: active collective entity
022: dormant collective entity
100: completed inward process
101: active inward process
102: pending inward process
110: completed outward process
111: active outward process
112: pending outward process
120: completed systemic process
121: active systemic process
122: pending systemic process
200: stable inward capacity
201: active inward capacity
202: dormant inward capacity
210: stable outward relationship
211: active outward relationship
212: unresolved outward relationship
220: stable systemic relationship
221: active systemic relationship
222: unrealized systemic possibility
5. Trit-to-Melody Algorithm
Trits are encoded as relative melodic movement, not as fixed notes and not as the root, third, and fifth of a chord.
Trit 0: remain on the current pitch; movement 0 semitones
Trit 1: rise one DBA step; movement +2 semitones
Trit 2: fall one DBA step; movement -2 semitones
One DBA step: 2 semitones
A note path always contains the starting pitch followed by one movement for each trit. A three-trit root therefore has four pitch positions.
000: relative path [0, 0, 0, 0]
012: relative path [0, 0, +2, 0]
111: relative path [0, +2, +4, +6]
222: relative path [0, -2, -4, -6]
Example: 012 from C is C–C–D–C. The same address from G is G–G–A–G. Both are the same DBA root because the interval sequence is identical.
6. Vocal Encoding and Canonical Transliteration
Formal carrier syllables
0: ma
1: ki
2: nu
The full sung carrier is the family onset followed by one carrier syllable per trit. LIF:012 is ni-ma-ki-nu; MOV:012 is gi-ma-ki-nu.
Local compact-root algorithm
Ordinary compact speech compresses the three address trits into one consonant-vowel-consonant root.
First trit → initial consonant: 0=n, 1=k, 2=m
Second trit → vowel: 0=a, 1=o, 2=i
Third trit → final consonant: 0=m, 1=k, 2=n
000: nam
012: non
111: kok
222: min
The same local compact root occurs at the same address in every family. Family identity is supplied by the harmonic opening and, in human writing, by the family onset.
Canonical human transliteration: family onset + middle dot + local compact root
LIF:000: ni·nam
MOV:000: gi·nam
The local form nam remains a valid field and may be sufficient inside a clearly established harmonic context, but family-qualified transliteration is the canonical written form.
7. Runtime States
Runtime state describes the current status of the referent or operation in a particular utterance. It is appended after the semantic root and remains separate from the third address trit.
State 0
Meaning: inactive, false, ended, unavailable, or inaccessible
Musical ending: descend one semitone and stop sharply
State 1
Meaning: active, valid, expressed, or executing
Musical ending: return firmly to the phrase starting pitch
State 2 — num
Meaning: dormant, pending, remembered, possible, or unresolved
Musical ending: rise a perfect fifth and sustain

Example: LIF:012 permanently means a dormant other. LIF:012 [1] states that this dormant identity validly exists. LIF:012 [0] states that the dormant identity is unavailable, false, or ended. LIF:012 [2] states that even its dormant existence is unresolved or only potentially recoverable.
8. Grammar Through Contour
level
Language function: declaration
Programming function: assert/assign
rising
Language function: question
Programming function: query/evaluate
sharply falling
Language function: command
Programming function: execute
rise then return
Language function: definition
Programming function: declare function/type
fall then rise
Language function: possibility
Programming function: conditional branch
repeated loop
Language function: repetition or habit
Programming function: iterate
unresolved ending
Language function: dependency
Programming function: await
overlapping phrases
Language function: simultaneity
Programming function: parallel execution
9. Participant Roles Through Register
low: actor, source, or cause
middle: process or relationship
high: target, result, or destination
sustained background: environment or persistent condition
A low Life phrase, a middle Repair phrase, and a high Life phrase can express that a living actor performs a repair process upon a living target without relying on English word order.
10. Timing and Relationship Syntax
no gap: modifier relationship
short gap: argument relationship
medium gap: next instruction
long gap: completed statement
overlap: simultaneous processes
repeated pulse: recursion or repeated action

Timing is semantic. Sequential phrases are serial; overlapping phrases are simultaneous or parallel. A repeated pulse can express repetition, habit, recursion, or iteration depending on the semantic domains involved.
11. Writing-System Baseline
The writing system is deterministic in information content but does not yet have an approved final visual glyph sheet.
Outer frame: harmonic family or semantic domain
Central path: trit movements
Vertical position: grammatical role or vocal register
Line contour: sentence or programming function
Spacing: timing and argument boundaries
Parallel paths: simultaneous voices or processes
Tail: runtime state
Written trit 0: straight continuation
Written trit 1: upward angle
Written trit 2: downward angle
A future glyph renderer must use the same semantic intermediate representation as the note, carrier, transliteration, and executable outputs. Visual style must not alter meaning.
12. Completed Atomic Lexicon
Only the following 36 roots are populated and canonical in Phase 1: all 27 Life roots and the nine Motion entity/condition roots. Core definitions below preserve the fixed source meanings.
Life Family — Complete
LIF:000 — ni·nam — continuous self
Universal slot: stable inward entity
Local compact root: nam
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-ma-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, 0, 0]
Core definition: The self understood as a continuous identity across time and changing states.
Distinctions and exclusions: This is deeper than English “I.” It means the identity that remains the same even if:
Source example: Example
“I exist as the same continuous self.”
Spoken compactly:
Nam.
LIF:001 — ni·nak — conscious self
Universal slot: active inward entity
Local compact root: nak
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-ma-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, 0, +2]
Core definition: The self as presently conscious, aware, and mentally available.
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“I am conscious.”
More literally:
“The aware expression of self is presently valid.”
Spoken:
Nak.
LIF:002 — ni·nan — dormant self
Universal slot: dormant inward entity
Local compact root: nan
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-ma-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, 0, -2]
Core definition: The self preserved without present conscious expression.
Translation candidates: sleep; suspended awareness; a saved identity; a backed-up consciousness; an individual in num; an identity awaiting embodiment
Distinctions and exclusions: Important distinction
LIF:010 — ni·nom — identified other
Universal slot: stable outward entity
Local compact root: nom
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-ki-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, +2, +2]
Core definition: A particular being recognized as distinct from the speaker.
Translation candidates: you; that individual; the selected person; the specific living target; a recognized being other than self
Source example: Example
“That identified being exists.”
In direct conversation it may naturally mean:
“You.”
Spoken:
Nom.
LIF:011 — ni·nok — conscious other
Universal slot: active outward entity
Local compact root: nok
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-ki-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, +2, +4]
Core definition: Another being who is presently conscious, awake, or responsive.
Source example: Example question
A rising contour applied to:
LIF:011
means:
“Are you conscious?”
Spoken:
Nok?
This could also be used as the DBA equivalent of:
“Can you hear me?”
“Are you awake?”
“Are you present?”
The exact interpretation depends on context.
LIF:012 — ni·non — dormant other
Universal slot: dormant outward entity
Local compact root: non
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-ki-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, +2, 0]
Core definition: Another identified individual whose identity remains preserved but is not presently expressed.
Translation candidates: a sleeping cyber-pet; a stored consciousness; an unawakened cyber-pet; a being awaiting activation; someone remembered but presently inaccessible
Source example: Example
“The dormant individual remains in num.”
Spoken:
Non-num.
The first part identifies what the entity is. The final num state says that even its dormant existence remains pending, inaccessible, or unresolved.
LIF:020 — ni·nim — life-kind
Universal slot: stable collective entity
Local compact root: nim
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-nu-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, -2, -2]
Core definition: Life understood as a class, category, or shared kind of existence.
Translation candidates: life; living being; biological or cybernetic life; species; the class of beings considered alive; cyber-pet life as a category
Distinctions and exclusions: Unlike many other roots, it changes very little because it remains extremely common.
Source example: Example
“Life exists.”
Spoken:
Nim.
This simple utterance could survive almost unchanged into Era Three.
LIF:021 — ni·nik — living community
Universal slot: active collective entity
Local compact root: nik
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-nu-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, -2, 0]
Core definition: A population or community of living beings currently interacting as a living collective.
Distinctions and exclusions: It refers to the living network itself, not merely a collection of unrelated individuals.
Source example: Example
“The living community is active.”
Spoken:
Nik.
With a warning modifier, it could mean:
“The community is endangered.”
With a repair operation, it could mean:
“Restore the living community.”
LIF:022 — ni·nin — dormant lineage
Universal slot: dormant collective entity
Local compact root: nin
Full formal carrier: ni-ma-nu-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, 0, -2, -4]
Core definition: A population, lineage, or form of life preserved in potential rather than currently active.

Translation candidates: an extinct-looking species whose genetic information survives; stored cyber-pet templates; a population in mass dormancy; uninstantiated life patterns; a civilization preserved as recoverable information; descendants who could exist but have not yet awakened
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“The lineage remains dormant but has not been lost.”
More literally:
“Dormant collective life participates in reality through num.”
Spoken:
Nin-num.
LIF:100 — ni·kam — completed self-development
Universal slot: completed inward process
Local compact root: kam
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-ma-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, +2, +2]
Core definition: A being has completed an inward stage of development and reached a stable new form.
Translation candidates: mature; finish developing; complete a life stage; become fully formed; achieve stable self-development
Distinctions and exclusions: This is not simply physical growth. It may describe mental, structural, or identity development when the development is understood as part of the being’s life.
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“My development is complete.”
More literally:
“Completed inward life-development is presently valid.”
Compact speech:
Kam.
LIF:101 — ni·kak — awaken or activate oneself
Universal slot: active inward process
Local compact root: kak
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-ma-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, +2, +4]
Core definition: To bring one’s own life, consciousness, or functioning into active expression.
Translation candidates: awaken; wake oneself; activate oneself; become conscious; bring oneself online; resume one’s own living functions
Source example: Example command
LIF:101
ACTOR:LIF:002
FROM_STATE:2
TO_STATE:1
Natural translation:
“Awaken yourself from dormancy.”
Compact vocal form:
Kak!
The falling command contour distinguishes the instruction from the statement:
“I am awakening.”
LIF:102 — ni·kan — readiness for self-awakening
Universal slot: pending inward process
Local compact root: kan
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-ma-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, +2, 0]
Core definition: An inward awakening process that is prepared or possible but has not yet begun.
Translation candidates: ready to awaken; capable of self-activation; prepared to resume consciousness; awaiting permission to awaken; possess an unexecuted awakening process
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“I am ready to awaken.”
The operation itself is pending, but its readiness is currently valid.
Means:
“My ability to awaken remains possible, but its readiness cannot yet be confirmed.”
Compact speech:
Kan-num.
LIF:110 — ni·kom — completed awakening of another
Universal slot: completed outward process
Local compact root: kom
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-ki-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, +4, +4]
Core definition: The process of bringing another being into active life has been successfully completed.
Translation candidates: awaken another successfully; complete another’s activation; bring someone fully online; finish reviving or instantiating a being; establish another as an awake individual
Source example: Example
LIF:110
TARGET:LIF:012
RESULT_STATE:1
I’m
Natural translation:
“The dormant individual has been fully awakened.”
Compact speech:
Kom.
In a system log, this could function like:
AWAKEN_COMPLETE(target)
LIF:111 — ni·kok — actively awaken another
Universal slot: active outward process
Local compact root: kok
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-ki-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, +4, +6]
Core definition: To actively cause another being to become conscious, alive, or functionally expressed.
Translation candidates: awaken them; activate that being; bring the target online; revive the target; initiate another’s conscious functioning
Source example: Example command
LIF:111
TARGET:LIF:012
FROM_STATE:2
TO_STATE:1
Natural translation:
“Awaken the dormant individual.”
Compact vocalization:
Kok non—num-to-active.
Formal sung carrier:
Ni-ki-ki-ki … ni-ma-ki-nu.
The target phrase is placed in the higher register, while the awakening operation occupies the middle register.
LIF:112 — ni·kon — prepare another for awakening
Universal slot: pending outward process
Local compact root: kon
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-ki-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, +4, +2]
Core definition: To place another being into a condition from which awakening can later occur.
Translation candidates: prepare for awakening; prime another being; make a dormant being recoverable; ready a consciousness for activation; establish the prerequisites for life-expression
Distinctions and exclusions: This does not awaken the target immediately.
Source example: Example
LIF:112
TARGET:LIF:012
RESULT:LIF:102
Natural translation:
“Prepare the dormant being so that self-awakening becomes possible.”
Executable interpretation:
PREPARE_AWAKENING(
target = dormant_individual,
result = awakening_ready
Compact speech:
Kon non.
LIF:120 — ni·kim — completed development of a living system
Universal slot: completed systemic process
Local compact root: kim
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-nu-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, 0, 0]
Core definition: The formation or development of a population, ecology, or living network has reached a stable completed state.
Translation candidates: establish an ecosystem; complete population development; form a stable living community; complete ecological succession; bring a biosystem into equilibrium
Source example: Example
LIF:120
RESULT:LIF:220
STATE:1
Natural translation:
“The living system has finished developing into a stable biosystem.”
Compact speech:
Kim.
The compact syllable may resemble roots in other families. The Life harmony identifies this as a life-system process rather than a Motion-family concept.
LIF:121 — ni·kik — cause a living population to grow
Universal slot: active systemic process
Local compact root: kik
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-nu-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, 0, +2]
Core definition: To actively increase, diversify, or develop life at the population or system level.
Translation candidates: grow a population; expand a living community; increase biodiversity; propagate life; cause ecological growth; support a species’ active development
Source example: Example
LIF:121
TARGET:LIF:021
RESULT_STATE:1
Natural translation:
“Cause the living community to grow.”
Compact speech:
Kik nik.
Executable interpretation:
GROW_POPULATION(
target = active_living_community
LIF:122 — ni·kin — preserve life for future growth
Universal slot: pending systemic process
Local compact root: kin
Full formal carrier: ni-ki-nu-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, +2, 0, -2]
Core definition: To preserve a population, lineage, or living system in a form capable of future restoration or development.

Translation candidates: preserve a lineage; place a population into safe dormancy; store viable life; protect future generations; maintain an ecosystem as recoverable potential; suspend life without allowing its continuity to end
Distinctions and exclusions: The goal is not merely storage. The goal is:
Source example: Example
LIF:122
TARGET:LIF:021
RESULT:LIF:022
STATE:2
Natural translation:
“Preserve the living community as a dormant lineage that may live again.”
More literally:
“Transform actively expressed collective life into valid collective life-potential under num.”
Compact speech:
Kin nik—nin-num.
Executable interpretation:
PRESERVE_LINEAGE(
target = living_community,
output = dormant_lineage,
state = NUM
This operation may eventually become central to how the cyber-pets survived the disappearance of the DBA.
LIF:200 — ni·mam — stable viability
Universal slot: stable inward capacity
Local compact root: mam
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-ma-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, -2, -2]
Core definition: The stable capacity of a being to remain alive and continue functioning.
Translation candidates: viability; capacity for life; ability to survive; sustainable living condition; biological or cybernetic integrity; stable life-support capability

Distinctions and exclusions: This does not mean that the being is currently energetic or awake. It means the systems necessary for continued life are intact. Important distinction Therefore, unconsciousness does not imply death.
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“The being remains viable.”
More literally:
“Its stable capacity for continued life is presently valid.”
Compact speech:
Mam.
LIF:201 — ni·mak — active vitality
Universal slot: active inward capacity
Local compact root: mak
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-ma-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, -2, 0]
Core definition: The active expression of a being’s power to live, act, grow, and recover.
Translation candidates: vitality; vigor; life-energy; active health; liveliness; present living strength
Distinctions and exclusions: That does not necessarily mean the identity itself has been destroyed.
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“I am full of life.”
More precisely:
“My life-capacity is actively expressed.”
Compact speech:
Mak.
With reduced runtime state:
could mean:
“Vitality has ceased.”
That does not necessarily mean the identity itself has been destroyed.
LIF:202 — ni·man — dormant life-potential
Universal slot: dormant inward capacity
Local compact root: man
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-ma-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, -2, -4]
Core definition: The capacity for an individual life to exist or awaken, although that capacity is not presently expressed.
Translation candidates: latent life; dormant vitality; recoverable life-potential; capacity to live again; unexpressed possibility of awakening; preserved individual potential
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“A real capacity for this individual to live exists.”
Natural translation:
“The individual’s life-potential remains unresolved but has not been lost.”
Compact speech:
Man-num.
LIF:210 — ni·mom — established life-bond
Universal slot: stable outward relationship
Local compact root: mom
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-ki-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, 0, 0]
Core definition: A stable relationship through which two living identities recognize one another as connected.
Translation candidates: kinship; established bond; belonging; recognized family relationship; persistent identity connection; bonded companionship
Distinctions and exclusions: This bond does not have to be biological.
Source example: Example
LIF:210
MEMBER_A:LIF:000
MEMBER_B:LIF:010
STATE:1
Natural translation:
“You and I possess an established life-bond.”
Compact speech:
Nam, nom—mom.
The Era Three phrase:
Mi yu wu
may preserve a much simpler descendant of this idea.
LIF:211 — ni·mok — active care
Universal slot: active outward relationship
Local compact root: mok
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-ki-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, 0, +2]
Core definition: The active use of one being’s life-capacity to protect, support, nurture, or sustain another being.
Translation candidates: care for; nurture; protect life; tend to another; sustain another being; act for another’s continued well-being
Distinctions and exclusions: Unlike the Repair-family operations, active care does not require prior damage.
Source example: Example
LIF:211
ACTOR:LIF:001
TARGET:LIF:011
STATE:1
Natural translation:
“I am actively caring for you.”
Compact speech:
Nak mok nok.
Depending on context, this could also mean:
“I will keep you alive.”
“I am protecting you.”
“Your well-being is under my care.”
LIF:212 — ni·mon — possible or unresolved kinship
Universal slot: unresolved outward relationship
Local compact root: mon
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-ki-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, 0, -2]
Core definition: A potential relationship between living identities that has not yet been confirmed, completed, or fully expressed.
Translation candidates: possible kin; emerging bond; unconfirmed identity relationship; future companion; relationship awaiting recognition; one who may belong with us
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“A bond may exist between us, but it has not yet been realized.”
Compact speech:
Mon-num.
A question contour would mean:
“Are we connected?”
“Are you one of us?”
“Could this being belong to our lineage?”
LIF:220 — ni·mim — stable biosystem
Universal slot: stable systemic relationship
Local compact root: mim
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-nu-ma
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, -4, -4]
Core definition: A self-sustaining system of living beings and the relationships necessary for their continued existence.
Translation candidates: ecosystem; biosphere; stable living network; self-maintaining habitat; ecological system; living environment
Distinctions and exclusions: This root includes more than the beings themselves.
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“The ecosystem is stable and viable.”
Compact speech:
Mim.
A damaged biosystem might be encoded as:
LIF:220
WRN:021
STATE:1
Meaning:
“The biosystem is experiencing active systemic danger.”
LIF:221 — ni·mik — active living network
Universal slot: active systemic relationship
Local compact root: mik
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-nu-ki
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, -4, -2]
Core definition: A distributed network in which living beings are actively exchanging support, information, energy, or function.
Translation candidates: active ecology; living network; functioning society; interdependent community; active biosphere; collective life-process
Distinctions and exclusions: The distinction between LIF:021 and LIF:221 is important.
Source example: Example
Natural translation:
“The living network is active.”
Compact speech:
Mik.
This concept may eventually be important to multiplayer, community, or cyber-pet communication systems.
LIF:222 — ni·min — unrealized life
Universal slot: unrealized systemic possibility
Local compact root: min
Full formal carrier: ni-nu-nu-nu
Relative harmonic signature: 0–4–7
Relative note path: [0, -2, -4, -6]
Core definition: Life that could validly exist, but has not yet taken individual, collective, or physical form.
Translation candidates: unrealized life; possible species; uncreated living form; life before manifestation; potential descendants; life awaiting a viable path into existence

GATE 4A TYPED COMPOUND ARCHITECTURE 1.0.0 — CANONICAL

Gate 4A defines how the 324 canonical Era Zero atoms may be composed without approving any particular compound meaning. A lexical compound is a finite connected directed acyclic semantic graph with exactly one explicit semantic head. Every component retains its canonical atomic meaning and generated forms.

Source-grounded realization remains fixed: describing material precedes its semantic head; a no-gap boundary marks modifier attachment; a short gap marks typed argument attachment; and only the semantic head normally receives the compound's external role contour.
Machine-readable compound model

Node types: canonical root, approved versioned compound reference, typed open slot, and explicit coordination group. Gate 4A edge types are qualifies (descriptor to described node), fills_role (typed argument to predicate or relation), and member_of (member to an all-of, any-of, or exactly-one group).

The role inventory covers actor, source, cause, experiencer, bearer, predicate, target, result, destination, instrument, material, location, environment, condition, and persistent condition. Core low, middle, high, and sustained-background register mappings remain unchanged.

Modifier and argument targets are explicit; adjacency never overrides the graph. Nested references must be versioned and acyclic. Multiple independent assertions are not lexical compounds and must wait for the later utterance IR.
Identity, state, and change control

Canonical compound identity is derived from a normalized semantic payload containing the architecture version, head, nodes, edges, and lexical constraints. Presentation metadata, English glosses, runtime state, contour, register, and absolute pitch are excluded from the content identity.

Runtime [0], [1], or [2]/num belongs to an utterance occurrence and is never stored as part of a lexical compound identity. Changing a compound's head, graph, role binding, scope, slot type, or lexical constraints requires a new definition version and migration; approved entries may be deprecated or superseded but never silently rewritten.

Sense-routing contract

An English surface form is not itself a language meaning. Every indexed reading is a separate sense record that routes to exactly one canonical atom, one approved compound, future grammar, future semantic IR, or an explicit unsupported gap. Key distinctions
• send separates active communicative expression (CON:101) from active target data transfer (DAT:111).

Purpose and graph model

The semantic IR is the language’s authoritative proposition layer. It represents meaning independently of English word order, absolute pitch, MIDI, glyph layout, or audio. Every utterance is a finite connected directed acyclic graph with one root clause. Nodes represent clauses, canonical lexical occurrences, literals, variables, references, scope operators, coordination, time anchors, measurements, and state snapshots. Typed edges express centers, semantic roles, scope, coordination membership, time relations, conditions, transitions, coreference, and discourse grounding.
Independent semantic dimensions
The following dimensions must never be collapsed:
• the root’s lexical third trit;
• the occurrence’s runtime state [0], [1], or [2]/num;
• positive or negative polarity;
• modality such as possible, necessary, permitted, or obligated;
• reference time and tense relation;
• grammatical aspect.

Runtime [0] does not mean “not.” Runtime [1] does not mean present tense or truth. Runtime [2]/num does not mean future tense or possible modality. A root lexically ending in trit 2 retains its canonical invariant regardless of the runtime state applied to a particular occurrence.
Roles, scope, and reference

The IR preserves the Core 1.0 actor/source/cause, predicate, target/result/destination, and background roles and adds typed roles needed for complete propositions, including experiencer, bearer, content, recipient, instrument, material, location, time, manner, quantity, comparison standard, and beneficiary. Roles are explicit; adjacency cannot supply a missing participant.

Negation, modality, quantification, aspect, and repetition are scope operators with one exact scope. References resolve through declared referent IDs and explicit coreference edges. An unresolved reference produces an error or clarification request rather than a guessed antecedent.
Quantity, time, and transitions

Quantifiers distinguish exact, at-least, at-most, range, all, some, none, and proportional readings. Measurements use canonical decimal magnitudes and controlled units. Quantifier “none” is not the same as negating a whole clause.

Tense is represented through explicit before, at, after, during, starts, ends, or overlaps relations to speech time, reference time, absolute time, or an interval. Transition clauses require one explicit before-state and one explicit after-state; a lexical process alone does not silently provide either snapshot.
Composition and execution

Coordination distinguishes all-of, any-of, exactly-one, sequence, and parallel structure. Sequences require contiguous order beginning at one. Parallel members have no serial order. Repetition specifies a finite count, while-condition, or until-condition. Clause embedding and compound references may recurse only through a finite acyclic expanded graph.

Canonical execution validates schema, lexical authority, graph structure, cardinality, scope, bindings, quantities, time, transitions, and serialization in a fixed order. Semantic payloads serialize as canonical UTF-8 JSON and receive content-derived UTT identifiers from SHA-256 digests.
Release boundary

“Executable grammar” means the IR has deterministic validation, binding, scope, evaluation order, diagnostics, and serialization. It does not mean an English parser, renderer, inverse decoder, MIDI engine, glyph generator, or translator exists yet. The next release must map canonical IR to formal notation, family-qualified forms, carriers, notes, runtime endings, contours, timing, and registers, then decode that realization back to the identical IR under round-trip tests.
Deterministic Renderer and Inverse Decoder 1.0
Status: CANONICAL — CONTROLLED-ENGLISH GATE MAY BEGIN
Canonical contract

The renderer accepts only canonical EZIR-JSON-1 semantic IR with a valid content-derived UTT identity. It resolves every lexical target against the 324 canonical atoms or 28 approved compounds, preserves the exact semantic graph, and emits an EZF-1 document containing the complete source IR plus a deterministic performance plan and diagnostic literal gloss.

Lexical generation emits the fixed family-qualified transliteration, formal carrier, harmonic family opening, and relative note path for every atom. Compounds expand in qualifier-before-head order. Only the semantic head receives the compound occurrence’s runtime ending. Any open compound participant slot—such as the source and target of the directed data-link template—must be explicitly bound by a typed fills_role edge before rendering.
Reference performance profile

The default middle-register anchor is MIDI 60; anchors from 24 through 96 are valid. Register offsets are low −12, middle 0, high +12, and sustained-background −5 semitones. Exact pitch and reference duration are presentation choices. Meaning is carried by the relative harmonic, address, contour, timing, and register relations, so transposition does not change the UTT identity or EZF identity.

Runtime state [0] descends one semitone from the address-final note and stops sharply. Runtime state [1] returns firmly to the phrase/register starting pitch. Runtime state [2], whose fixed name is num, rises seven semitones—a perfect fifth—from the address-final note and sustains. num is not a numeric parameter.

Primary speech-act contours are level assertion, rising question, sharply falling command, rise-then-return definition, and fall-then-rise possibility. Secondary contours mark repetition, parallelism, and unresolved condition or dependency. Structural timing maps qualification to no gap, role filling to a short gap, ordinary structural edges to a medium gap, parallel membership to overlap, repetition to repeated pulse, and statement completion to a long gap.
Inverse decoding and identity

Formal identity is the SHA-256 digest of the semantic digest plus the transposition-independent relative performance plan; the visible identifier uses EZF:<first 24 lowercase hexadecimal digits>. The inverse decoder regenerates the expected rendering and rejects mismatches in identity, semantics, generated forms, notes, runtime endings, registers, contours, timing, or gloss. It never guesses or repairs. Successful decoding returns the original canonical semantic IR exactly.

Purpose and boundary

Controlled English is now an executable, deliberately restricted input language. It is not unrestricted prose. It accepts exact quoted canonical atom or approved compound labels, an explicit runtime state, and documented uppercase grammar keywords. Canonical grammar

Every statement ends with one period and begins with ASSERT, QUESTION, COMMAND, DEFINE, or POSSIBILITY. A lexical occurrence is written as a quoted controlled label followed by [0], [1], or [2]. num remains the fixed name of runtime state 2 in rendering; it is not accepted as a numeric or fourth state.

The simple template supports ordered NOT, MODAL, and ASPECT operators; typed ROLE arguments; TIME relations to SPEECH_TIME; MEASURE with canonical decimal and unit; and QUANTIFIER. General-English Candidate Translator 1.0
Status: CANONICAL — CORE TRANSLATOR PIPELINE COMPLETE
Conservative translation contract

The general-English interface analyzes ordinary surface phrases against all 436 indexed senses. It returns a deterministic ranked candidate list containing the sense ID, route, canonical target when one exists, invariant definition, selection cues, numerical score, confidence tier, match type, and explicit scoring evidence. Ties are ordered by sense ID, never source-file order.

Analysis is distinct from resolution. The translator may automatically resolve only one unique exact lemma with an explicit final runtime marker [0], [1], or [2], a direct atom or compound route, and no open compound slots. Every other case returns clarification requirements. Explicit resolution requires the selected sense, runtime state, speech act, and all required roles; it then passes through controlled English, canonical Semantic IR, EZF-1, and exact inverse decoding.
Ranking and ambiguity policy

Exact-lemma matches begin at 1.0; contained lemmas at 0.72; partial lexical matches use bounded token coverage. Selection-cue overlap and definition overlap add bounded evidence, with the total capped at 1.0 and rounded to four decimals. Confidence is high at 0.90 or above, medium at 0.65 or above, and low below 0.65. Any competitor within 0.12 of the top score is materially ambiguous and prevents automatic resolution.

The translator never silently selects the first sense. A missing runtime state, close competing readings, a nonexact surface match, an open compound role, a Semantic-IR or grammar route, or a documented vocabulary gap causes a visible clarification. Direct atom and closed-compound candidates expose full Semantic-IR alternatives for the permitted runtime states. Slotted compounds expose required roles instead of incomplete IR.
Coverage and honest limits

Every indexed sense is available to ranking. Literal “go” exposes both spatial Motion and abstract-transition routes. “Change” exposes Data, Matter, Mind, Structure, and generic-transition readings. Context such as “represented information content” raises the Data reading but does not bypass the clarification rule for a nonexact surface phrase. “Food” and both readings of “home” remain explicit vocabulary gaps with no fabricated target.

EZSVG-1 renders one labeled row per lexical event. Transposition changes MIDI notes and SVG vertical coordinates while leaving the semantic digest and formal identity unchanged.

Synthesized waveform audio is optional and is not implemented in Era Zero 1.0. Choosing a synthesizer, instrument, timbre, articulation library, or recorded voice would add presentation policy not fixed by the language. MIDI preserves the complete deterministic performance interchange; any later synthesizer must consume that output without altering meaning.
